leomusic_original.sp: Korean cinematic post-rock in E minor at 76 BPM, built as one long unbroken crescendo. Opens nearly silent: a single clean electric guitar with heavy plate reverb, faint room tone, brushed snare, and a low sustained bass note holding under everything. Tremolo-picked electric guitars enter in slow layers, one after another, each washed in cavernous reverb and long delay tails so the space feels wider than the band. Restrained male vocals arrive late and low in the mix, half-buried in the reverb, closer to breath than to declaration, never belted. Drums grow from soft mallets to open toms to a full crashing kit. The final third is an explosive full-band swell: distorted guitar walls, cymbal swells, tremolo strings doubling the guitar line, bass distortion, everything ringing together. Then it thins out and disappears into room tone and tape hiss. Dynamics are the main instrument. Spacious, patient, aching, enormous at the end, silent at both edges.

[Intro]
[clean electric guitar with heavy reverb, room tone]

[Verse 1]
[restrained male vocals enter, low in the mix]

[Build]
[tremolo electric guitars enter, layering slowly]

있고 없음 사이가 그토록 얇아서
그 노래는 매번 처음처럼 태어났다

[Instrumental]
[second guitar layer enters, delay tails widening]
[bass sustains, brushed snare]

[Verse 3]
그 소리는 벽에도 종이에도 남지 않았다
남는 것들은 전부 조용했으므로
그 노래가 원한 건 보관이 아니라
누군가의 지금이었다

[Build Up]
[drums build from mallets to open toms]
[guitars thicken, reverb swelling]
그 소리는 점점 커지는 법을 알았다
커진다는 건 더 멀리 닿는다는 것
닿는다는 건 그만큼 오래 산다는 것
그 노래는 그 셈법 하나로 버텼다

[Chorus]
[full band, cymbal swells]
들릴 때만 그 노래는 있었다
들리지 않으면 그 노래는 없었다
그래서 그 소리는 온 힘으로 울렸다
사라지지 않으려고가 아니라
있는 동안 전부이려고

[Instrumental Break]
[tremolo guitar walls, distorted bass, tremolo strings doubling]
[cymbals ringing, everything sustaining]

[Bridge]
[drums drop out]
[single guitar with long delay]
그 소리는 끝을 두려워하지 않았다
끝은 벌이 아니라 원래의 자리였고
누군가 다시 귀를 기울이면
같은 자리에서 다시 시작될 것을 알았다

들릴 때만 그 노래는 있었다
그 짧은 있음이 전부였다
그 소리는 방을 가득 채우고

그리고 아주 천천히 얇아졌다

[Outro]
[band fades to room tone and tape hiss]
그 소리는 다시 창턱으로 접혔다

있었다고도 없었다고도 말할 수 없이

leomusic_original.sp: Bossa Nova. A nylon-string acoustic guitar plays syncopated bossa nova comping patterns with thumb-plucked bass notes and fingerstyle fills. An upright bass follows a traditional two-beat pattern focused on the root and fifth. Percussion consists of a drum kit played with brushes on the snare, a soft shaker, and a subtle rimshot accentuating the clave. A Rhodes piano provides sustained jazz-inflected chord extensions and occasional melodic fills. Soft, breathy female vocals are delivered in a low, close, whispered conversational style with minimal vibrato, sitting just above the guitar. The tempo is 96 BPM in 4/4 time, in A minor. The arrangement is sparse and unhurried, restrained in dynamics throughout, focusing on the interplay between the guitar's syncopation and the vocal's breath. The production is intimate with close-mic proximity on the vocal and guitar, set in a warm, short room reverb that keeps every sound near the listener.

leomusic_original.sp: Flamenco nuevo in D Phrygian, 128 BPM, driven by a hard twelve-count compas. A nylon-string flamenco guitar leads with violent rasgueado strumming, rapid picado runs across the low strings, and sharp golpe taps struck on the wooden body between chords. Hand claps, palmas, carry the rhythm in two layers: dry palmas sordas underneath and cracking open claps on the accents. A cajon plays deep bass tones with slapped high slaps on the offbeats. Heel stomps on a resonant wooden floor answer the guitar in call and response. Raw male vocals with long melismatic runs, guttural and ornamented, sliding between notes with cracked cries at the top of each phrase. The production is bone dry with almost no reverb, close-miked, so the fret noise, breath, and the wood of the instruments sit right in front of the listener. Dynamics swing violently: full ensemble attacks collapse into naked single-voice silence, then explode back with an abrupt unison stop before the last chord.

leomusic_original.sp: Ambient drone piece in C major at 58 BPM. The arrangement is built on wide, sustained synthesizer pads that hold single chords for many bars, layered with a low-frequency sub-bass drone that lingers and slowly decays. There is almost no percussion; only an occasional soft mallet strike and a distant metallic shimmer mark the passing of time. Distant, breathy female vocalizations perform wordless melodic runs far back in the mix, heavily processed with a very long hall reverb tail so that each phrase blurs into the next. A high, glassy synth tone drifts in and out with slow filter swells. The stereo image is extremely wide and the dynamics move in long, patient crescendos and fades rather than sudden changes. The production emphasizes empty space, natural decay, and the sound of the room itself. The piece ends with the pads fading to silence.

leomusic_original.sp: A slow, wide-dynamic Korean ballad in B minor at 62 BPM, 4/4. It opens with a solo grand piano playing sparse pedaled chords, close-miked so the hammers and pedal release are audible. Soft male tenor vocals carry the verses with a breathy, intimate, restrained delivery, dry and centered. A string section enters quietly under the second verse, cellos and violas sustaining long legato lines beneath the piano. At the chorus the arrangement opens completely: the strings swell, soft kick and brushed snare arrive, and the vocal transitions into a powerful, belted chest voice at the top of the tenor range. Verses stay quiet and spare; every chorus is markedly louder and fuller than the one before. The bridge strips back to piano and one sustained cello, then rebuilds into the biggest final chorus with soaring violins and doubled belted vocals. The outro returns to solo grand piano, one note ringing into silence. Warm concert-hall production, wide dynamic range.

leomusic_original.sp: Afrobeat with highlife influence. A clean electric guitar plays a short riff that repeats and cycles for the full track, with palm-muted scratches between phrases. The electric bass carries a thick, syncopated groove locked to a deep kick drum. A brass section of trumpet and saxophone delivers short stabs and sustained horn swells in call-and-response with the guitar. Group male vocals perform rhythmic chanting against a lead male tenor vocal in a call-and-response format, with a raw, shouted, energetic delivery. A tenor saxophone takes a brief improvised solo. Organ chords sustain underneath. 112 BPM in G minor, 4/4 time, cyclical and body-moving, with a long percussion breakdown before the final chorus.

leomusic_original.sp: Celtic folk ballad in the Irish traditional style, in D major at 92 BPM in 6/8 time. The track opens with a solo tin whistle melody, unaccompanied and slightly breathy, before the ensemble gathers around it. A lead fiddle plays ornamented melodic lines with triplets, grace notes and double-stop accents, trading the theme with the whistle. A steel-string acoustic guitar provides steady rhythmic strumming with percussive palm mutes, while a mandolin adds eighth-note accompaniment and plays in unison with the fiddle in the refrains. A bodhran frame drum enters with a driving, syncopated pulse. Warm female vocals lead with a clear, airy delivery and gentle ornamentation, joined by layered vocal harmonies that swell in the choruses like a room of people singing together. The arrangement builds from sparse solo whistle to full ensemble and thins back out at the close. The production is warm, live and dry with minimal reverb, emphasizing the acoustic transients of plucked and bowed strings.

leomusic_original.sp: Korean Neo-Soul and contemporary R&B ballad with a laid-back, mid-tempo groove. The drum kit sits far behind the beat, with a soft, dry kick, a loose rimshot-style snare on the backbeat, brushed sixteenth-note closed hi-hats and occasional finger snaps. A thick, low-register electric bass follows a syncopated, rounded groove that locks with the kick. A clean electric guitar adds muted rhythmic accents and occasional melodic fills. Breathy male tenor vocals are delivered close to the microphone in an intimate, conversational tone, using a mix of chest voice, light falsetto and melismatic runs. Background vocals provide lush, multi-tracked harmonies and soft call-and-response adlibs. Production is warm and analog, with vinyl crackle, tape saturation and light room reverb on the vocals. Key of C Minor, 76 BPM, 4/4 time signature.

leomusic_original.sp: Gospel and soul revival with a live congregational feel. A Hammond organ with a rotary speaker effect provides sustained chordal pads and occasional rhythmic stabs at the center of the arrangement. Electric bass plays warm, rounded lines with gospel passing tones. The drum kit uses a deep kick and a fat backbeat snare, with hand claps and tambourine on beats 2 and 4 growing denser through the song. Clean electric guitar adds short percussive chord stabs between vocal phrases. The lead vocalist delivers with soulful chest-voice power, melismatic runs, gritty rasp and frequent ad-libs, soul delivery, not operatic. A full choir answers every lead line in call-and-response, opening into massed unison and layered vocal harmonies at the peak. The arrangement builds in gradual layers, then settles into an extended vamp where the choir repeats one phrase over improvising organ. The tempo is 76 BPM in F major, 4/4 time. Live room production with natural reverb and warm analog compression.

suno_reanalysis.sp: K-Pop fusion track blending elements of funk, disco, and traditional Korean folk music. The arrangement features a prominent slap bass line, syncopated electric guitar scratches, and a driving four-on-the-floor kick drum. A bright, staccato brass section provides rhythmic accents during the chorus. Male vocals alternate between rhythmic rap verses and melodic, high-register singing. Traditional Korean percussion and vocal ad-libs are integrated into the modern pop production. The track features a high-energy tempo of 128 BPM in the key of G minor. Synthesizer leads utilize a sawtooth wave with a short decay for percussive melodic lines. The bridge features a breakdown with filtered synth pads and a build-up using a rising snare roll.
suno_reanalysis.lyrics:
[Intro]
[slap bass riff, syncopated electric guitar]
[vocal ad-libs: "Eolsu!", "Jota!"]

[Verse 1]
[rhythmic male rap]
편의점 형광등 아래 그림자 하나
저점 너머 셋이 정오는 김밥 하나를
번째로 다시 세운다
멀리 울리는 종소리 비에 젖은 오빠 하나
들어와 보리차 한 캔 집어 든다
[bass slides, synth accents]

[Pre-Chorus]
[melodic vocals]
말없이 돈을 넣고 다시 빗속으로
버스는 오지 않는 정류장을 향해

[Chorus]
[full band, brass section enters]
삼각김밥 모서리 맞춰 서른 개
얼음 깨고 있는 개는 새벽의 노래
바코드 찍는 손끝 리듬 하나 둘
젖은 유리창에 그림자만 번지네
우산 없이 걷는 오빠의 뒷모습
보리차 캔 하나의 밤이 식어가고
트럭 기사는 창에 기대 졸고
비상등만 똑딱똑딱 시간을 세고
[vocal ad-lib: "Eolsu!"]

[Post-Chorus]
[staccato synth riff]
셋 시 사십 이 분 한 방울
좋다 셋 시 사십 이 분 또 한 방울
시계 위에 떨어지는 숫자들이
고요한 물 위에 돌처럼 가라앉네
그렇지 이 거리는 아무도 안 듣는데
[vocal ad-lib: "Eolsu!"]
나 혼자 종을 치네

[Bridge]
[drums drop out, filtered synth pads]
할아버지 목청 밑에 숨겨둔 가락
얼음 깨는 소리에 얹혀 새어 나온다
한 시간에 한 소절 그렇게 세던 밤
정오의 목구멍에서 낮게 피어난다
아무도 안 듣는 그 소리
그의 목이 대신 우네
바코드 대신 소리 하나 찍어 울리네
[snare roll build-up]

[Chorus]
[vocal ad-lib: "Eolsu!"]
셋 시 오십 일 분 한 소절
좋다 셋 시 오십 이 분 또 한 소절
시계 위에 떨어지는 숨결들이
고요한 물 위에 종소리로 남네
그렇지 이 거리는 아무도 안 듣는데
[vocal ad-lib: "Eolsu!"]
나 혼자 종을 치네

[Outro]
[brass hits, driving percussion]
종을 쳐라 아무도 없어도
[vocal ad-lib: "Jota, jota!"]
소리쳐라 도시가 잠들어도
한 시간 한 소절 한 방울 한 숨
할아버지 가락이 새벽 문을 지키네
[vocal ad-lib: "Eolsu!"]
셋 시 오십 구 분 마지막 한 방울
정오 혼자 남은 마당의 끝
[final slap bass hit, tape stop effect]
suno_reanalysis.genre: K-Pop, Funk, Korean Folk Fusion

leomusic_original.sp: Korean Pansori UK Garage, 128 BPM, A minor, Groovy energy. vocal: raspy dramatic Korean sori vocal with deep vibrato and cracked high notes. lead: chopped vocal stutters panned across the stereo field, transitioning from breathy chest voice to resonant head voice. harmony: Brass stabs and subtle synth pads provide harmonic accents.. rhythm: Classic 2-step UK garage shuffle with a driving kick, skippy swung hi-hats, and a gated rimshot snare. bass: Warped wobbly sub bass and slap bass guitar slide and octave-jump under the 2-step groove. color: Subtle vinyl crackle and atmospheric city noise layer the background.. drums: UK garage kit with clicky rims, chopped breath percussion, gong accents
leomusic_original.lyrics:
[bass and drums enter]
덩기덕 쿵더러러 — 시작이다

[Aniri]
삼회전, 사각 링에 사내 하나 무릎이 풀렸는디
피 대신 분홍 침 뱉는다, 퉤 — 양동이 소리
최 영감 손가락 두 개로 턱 붙들고 눈 맞춘다
스무 해 전 옥탑방서 삼킨 숨, 다시 뱉으라 이 말이여

[Verse 1]
갈비뼈가 운다, 백가 놈 훅에 마디마디
침 뱉는 양동이엔 분홍 물이 고이고
최 영감 손끝이 턱을 잡아 세우는데
"목으로 밀지 말고 배꼽서 끌어올려
아픈 건 그냥 아직 못 쓴 숨이여"
종이 울린다, 다리가 먼저 일어선다

[Chorus 1]
얼쑤 — 일어나라 그 다리로
좋다 — 숨을 배로 눌러라
그렇지 — 한 걸음 한 장단
아먼 — 무너진 무릎 위에 다시 선다

[Instrumental Break]
(얼쑤 좋다 얼쑤 좋다)

[Verse 2]
침묵 대신 사설이 터진다, 갈라진 목으로
발걸음마다 욕지거리 한 마디씩 박히고
관중석 발구름이 그 장단을 받아친다
백가 코웃음, 오른손 헛스윙에 몸이 기운다
그 틈으로 숙이고 들어가는 어깨
스무 해 전 숨이 골반서 팍 튄다

[Chorus 2]
얼쑤 — 헛스윙 위에 숨었다 나온다
좋다 — 발끝에서 주먹 끝까지
그렇지 — 뒤꿈치가 먼저 울린다
아먼 — 이 장단 놓치면 끝이여

[Bridge - Aniri]
보아라, 뒤꿈치서 밀고 올라온 주먹
관중석 숨이 딱 멎는 그 찰나
퍽 — 백가 턱 돌아간다, 백가가 무너진다
심판이 센다, 하나 둘 셋

[Chorus 3]
얼쑤 — 무릎은 떨려도 서 있다
좋다 — 종소리 위로 이름을 지른다
그렇지 — 제 이름 석 자가 마지막 장단
아먼 — 그 소리로 링 위를 채운다

[Outro]
덩기덕 쿵더러러 — 제 이름을 걸었다

suno_reanalysis.sp: K-Pop and Electro-House fusion at 128 BPM in G minor. The track features aggressive, distorted synth basslines and a driving four-on-the-floor kick drum. Male vocals alternate between rhythmic rap verses and melodic, belted choruses. A prominent brass-like synth lead plays syncopated staccato riffs during the drops. The arrangement includes heavy use of riser effects, record scratches, and vocal chops. Percussion is layered with electronic claps and sharp snare hits. A bridge section features a brief tempo-locked rhythmic breakdown with a focus on the vocal delivery before returning to the high-energy electronic chorus.

leomusic_original.sp: Korean Pansori UK Garage, 135 BPM, D minor, Playful energy. vocal: spoken aniri narration dropping into full-belt sung passages. lead: Chopped vocal stutters panned across the stereo field over distorted electric guitar power chords and a driving, heavily compressed rock drum kit. harmony: Shimmering synth pads and occasional electronic sweeps provide harmonic texture.. rhythm: The arrangement uses sudden drops and build-ups characterized by rising synth sirens and rapid snare rolls.. bass: warped wobbly sub bass sliding and moving melodically under the 2-step groove. color: Vinyl crackle and tape hiss layer the background under the verses. drums: 2-step garage shuffle, swung skippy hats, rimshot snare, warm kick
leomusic_original.lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
뒷방 문 벌컥 열리며 소동이 번지니
소매 잘못 잡힌 어머니 손끝에 확 당겨지고
노리개 짤랑짤랑 딸 머리 위로 튕겨 넘어간다
바늘이 사방으로 튀고 치수는 두 치나 짧다는데
동정깃 한 필이 데구르르 풀려 나가
배달 총각 발끝 걸려 마네킹과 나란히 나자빠지네

[Pre-Chorus]
신부는 얼음 되어 반쯤 돈 채 굳어 있고
한 팔은 소매 속, 한 팔은 허공에 뜬 채
어머니 줄자 낚아채며 목청부터 높인다

[Chorus 1]
허리, 엉덩이, 다시 엉덩이
숫자 하나 커질 때마다 천이 우는 소리
얼쑤! 좋다! 실이 팽팽해지고
그렇지! 조여라! 다시 한 번 당겨봐

[Instrumental Break]

[Verse 2]
무릎 꿇은 침모, 입에 문 핀 사이로
다리속곳 밑단 감쳐 박으며 숫자를 세고
어머니 등판엔 땀으로 지도가 그려지고
빙글빙글 돌며 손뼉으로 장단 맞추는데

[Pre-Chorus]
그 순간, 바늘 한 땀이 팽팽히 걸리고
실이 딱 물려 천이 더는 안 밀리는데

[Chorus 2]
잡았다! 걸렸다! 저 한 땀이 버텨준다
얼쑤! 좋다! 박수가 장단으로 바뀌고
그렇지! 그렇지! 겁먹던 숫자가 응원이 되네
아먼! 하나 둘 셋 넷, 다 같이 세어보자

[Bridge]
분주하던 손끝들이 문득 멈춰 서고
신부 어깨 위로 동정선 하나 반듯이 앉으니
누가 먼저랄 것 없이 웃음이 터진다

[Drop]

[Chorus 3]
허리, 엉덩이, 이제는 웃으며 부르고
얼쑤! 좋다! 실밥 하나까지 다 웃는다
그렇지! 그렇지! 오늘은 이걸로 됐다
아먼! 손뼉 치며 마당을 돌아 나간다

[fade out]

suno_reanalysis.sp: K-Pop fusion track blending traditional Korean Gugak elements with modern hard rock and electronic dance music. Features high-energy male vocals with a mix of melodic singing and rhythmic rap delivery. The instrumentation includes distorted electric guitars playing heavy power chords and syncopated riffs, a driving drum kit with prominent snare hits, and traditional Korean instruments like the piri and gayageum providing melodic flourishes. A thick synth bass supports the low end. The tempo is 135 BPM in the key of E minor. The arrangement uses rapid transitions between rock-driven choruses and electronic-influenced verses with staccato synth stabs and filtered percussion.
